Subject: Pen test asset inventory and report request

Hi Monica,

Thanks for the quick intro last week. As part of BrightSide's procurement review we need the following to complete our vendor assessment: 

- The most recent penetration test report (or a redacted executive summary) that covers Redwood-managed services.
- A current asset inventory for systems included in the test (service names, public endpoints, component versions).
- Clarification on which deployment types are included in your standard PT: Redwood-hosted API, Redwood-managed Dedicated reservations, Dedicated instances that run in a customer's cloud but are managed by Redwood, Private/VPC deployments, and on-prem packages.
- Current remediation status for any findings (high/critical) from the last test; if fixes are in progress, target ETA.

Can you confirm what you can provide and a target delivery date? We can accept a redacted PDF if full findings are too sensitive.

Thanks,
Daniel Wood
Security Manager, BrightSide AI

Hi Daniel — thanks for laying this out. Appreciated.

Short answers up front: we can provide a redacted PT executive summary and an asset inventory CSV. Scope needs a quick clarification from our security team (cc'd). Specifically: when you say "Dedicated instances that run in a customer's cloud but are managed by Redwood", do you mean (A) Redwood-managed runtime running on customer-provisioned VMs (we call this "customer-hosted Dedicated") or (B) Redwood-managed capacity in our own Dedicated pool that is logically assigned to the customer (we call this "Redwood-managed Dedicated")? The latter is in our standard PT scope; the former requires either (1) the customer contracts a scoped-onboarding PT with us or (2) we get permission to include the customer's infra in our test.

I'll loop security for definitions and remediation status; we should be able to turn around the redacted summary + inventory within 3 business days once we confirm scope. If you need the raw PT report (unredacted) we'll need an NDA amendment and an exchange process.

Best,
Monica Patel
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachments referenced: none in this message.

Monica — quick notes for the customer response: 

1) Standard Redwood PT scope (covered under our annual external engagement):
   - Redwood-hosted API endpoints (public control plane & inference endpoints)
   - Redwood-managed Dedicated pools (our infra where instances are provisioned and managed by Redwood)
   - Supporting public services (auth, telemetry ingestion endpoints, control plane components that we operate)

2) Out-of-scope by default unless explicitly contracted: 
   - Customer-hosted Dedicated (customer owned/provisioned instances running in their cloud where customer manages networking and some infra layers) — we can include these if the customer signs a scoped SOW and provides temporary testing access/permissions.
   - Private/VPC deployments: depends on deployment model: 
       * Private (Redwood Private with control plane still reachable/managed by Redwood) — the parts we manage (control plane components, update channels) are in scope; customer network/VPC endpoints are not tested without explicit consent.
       * On-prem packaged installs (air-gapped or fully customer-controlled) — scope is per-customer and typically excluded from our standard PT; we offer an add-on engagement.

3) Reports and redactions: we can provide an executive summary and a redacted findings report. Full, unredacted reports are available under an evidence-sharing agreement (we normally use a one-way NDA + secure transfer).

4) Remediation status: latest test (2026-07-01) had three findings classified as high; all three are closed in the fix tracker or have mitigation controls in place. We can export a remediation matrix showing status, PR links, and ETA for open items.

If you want, I can prepare the inventory CSV of assets that were in the 2026 test and a remediation matrix. Monica — target 72 hours to package the summary + inventory? 

-Rishi
Director, Security & Compliance

Hi Daniel — thanks again for the list. Short summary below and attached artifacts.

What we can provide now (attached):
- redwood-pt-summary-202609.pdf — redacted executive summary of the July 2026 external penetration test.
- asset-inventory-20260922.csv — asset/endpoint inventory for the systems included in the Redwood-managed scope.
- remediation-matrix-20260922.xlsx — status of high/critical findings and PR references.

Scope clarification (what is included by default):
- Redwood-hosted API (public, Redwood-operated) — included.
- Redwood-managed Dedicated pools (capacity we operate on behalf of customers) — included.

Out-of-scope unless contracted:
- Customer-hosted Dedicated (instances running on customer-provisioned cloud VMs where the customer controls networking) — not included unless we have scoped permission and a signed SOW.
- Private/VPC deployments — the Redwood-managed control plane components we operate are included; customer VPC networks and any customer-controlled nodes are excluded unless explicitly consented.
- On-prem packaged installs (air-gapped or fully customer-controlled) — excluded from standard engagement; available as a separate per-customer assessment.

Next steps / ask for BrightSide:
1) Confirm whether you want the redacted summary + inventory we attached (recommended) or the full unredacted report (requires an evidence-sharing agreement).
2) If you need inclusion of any customer-hosted Dedicated instances or Private/VPC endpoints, please confirm scope and timeline so we can prepare a scoped SOW.

Delivery ETA: attachments included now. If you confirm you need the unredacted report or additional scope, please let us know and we'll send the necessary legal steps and timeline.

Thanks — happy to jump on a 30-minute call if you'd like to review the inventory with our security team.

Best,
